Brazil election: Lula, Bolsonaro cast votes in final bout
Published October 25, 2026last updated October 25, 2026
Almost 160 million are eligible to vote in the final round of Brazil's election that pits the left-wing incumbent against the son of the former far-right president. DW has more.
What you need to know
- Brazilians are voting in the final round of the presidential election
- Left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is facing off against Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of the far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro
- Polls showed the two as neck-and-neck after Bolsonaro beat Lula by 2.2 million votes in the first round
- The 33 million voters who didn't vote in the first round could decide the result if they can be mobilized
Keep reading for the latest updates from the second round of Brazil's presidential election on Sunday, October 25:
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google. Then tap the "Star" or "Preferred" to keep DW News at the top of your feed.
What role is Trump playing in Brazil's election?
Although he hasn't endorsed either candidate, US President Donald Trump is close to the Bolsonaro family.
Not only did the senior Bolsonaro imitate Trump's rhetoric and policies, he also refused to concede defeat after losing to Lula in 2022, leading to his imprisonment for an attempted coup, provoking comparisons with Trump's own defeat to Joe Biden in 2020.
On the other side, Lula has presented himself as a defense against US interference.
The right "wants to govern with the American flag," Lula said after casting his ballot on Sunday.
A Bolsonaro win would mark a further move in Latin America toward pro-US far-right leaders, following in the footsteps of countries such as Colombia, Chile and Peru.
Results expected within hours of polls closing
The president of Brazil's Superior Electoral Court, Kassio Nunes Marques, has said he expects the winner of Sunday's vote to be announced officially between 8.30 p.m. and 9 p.m. (2330 and 0000 GMT), according to A Folha de Sao Paolo.
Brazil uses an electronic voting system meaning that ballots can be tallied quicker than in elections where paper votes are counted by hand.
However, the gap between the winner and loser is expected to be small, with the two running head-to-head in pre-election polls.
Supreme Court president urges candidates to accept result of vote
The head of Brazil's Supreme Federal Court, Edson Fachin, has called for the candidates to respect the result of Sunday's vote.
"It's important to remember that all authority and power comes from the people and, thus, it is fundamental that the choices that derive from the manifestation of popular sovereignty are respected," he said as he left his local polling station, according to A Folha de Sao Paulo.
"Brazil needs peace and calm to, from tomorrow, be able to confront the major challenges in many areas that demand the presence of the state."
Some observers have posited that Flavio Bolsonaro could refuse to accept a Lula victory, like his father before him, with the potential for violence to erupt.
IN DEPTH: What the election could mean for the Amazon
Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide.
With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.
Read DW's full story on the planet-sized consequences of Brazil's election.
WATCH: One community's divide over crime and policing
Rio's deadliest police raid left 122 people dead and divided a community. As voters weigh crime against police violence, Brazil's election battle is playing out in the streets of the district of Penha.
Flavio Bolsonaro urges Brazilians to vote 'rain or shine'
Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has urged voters to turn out "rain or shine" to change the country's direction, accusing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva of leaving Brazilians fearful.
"Brazil will change. Brazil will win," said the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, arguing that conditions had worsened over the past four years.
The opposition candidate criticized Lula's record on security and the economy, saying voters should not persist with a "mistake."
Bolsonaro cast his ballot at a school in Rio de Janeiro's Vila Isabel neighborhood around 20 minutes after polls opened. Wearing a yellow shirt, he arrived in the rain with his wife, Fernanda, amid heavy security.
Lula accuses Bolsonaro of preferring the US flag
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva says voters are choosing between a candidate who defends Brazil's flag and one who prefers the US flag, referring to his right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro.
The right "wants to govern with the American flag," the leftist incumbent said after casting his ballot in Sao Bernardo do Campo, near Sao Paulo.
Lula, who is seeking a fourth, nonconsecutive term, also said Brazilians had taken to the streets to defend their gains.
"What I saw in this runoff was not about a political party or a trade union. People took to the streets to defend their gains," he told reporters.
He also warned about political violence, citing a brick thrown at a supporter of his leftist Workers' Party (PT) in Montes Claros. "It shows what is at stake," he said.
Welcome to our coverage
Thank you for joining us today as we bring you the latest from the final round of Brazil's presidential election.
Polls opened at 8 a.m. this morning (1100 GMT) and are set to close at 5 p.m. (2000 GMT), based on time in the capital Brasilia. The first results are expected 30-60 minutes after polls close.
President Lula, 80, is hoping to turn around his defeat in the first round to Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro who is currently imprisoned for trying to overturn the previous election.
Flavio has said he would free his father if he wins and give him a role in his cabinet.

אזרחי ברזיל ניגשים לקלפיות בסיבוב השני של הבחירות לנשיאות במדינה, בקרב צמוד בין הנשיא המכהן מהשמאל לואיז אינסיו דה סילבה לבין פלביו בולסונארו, בנו של הנשיא לשעבר. הסקרים הראו שוויונות צמוד בין המועמדים, כאשר שיעור ההצבעה של מיליוני הבוחרים שנמנעו מהצבעה בסיבוב הראשון עשוי להכריע את תוצאות המערכה.

במהלך יום הבחירות התייחסו המועמדים לנושאים מדיניים וביטחוניים, כאשר לולה האשים את יריבו בהעדפת האינטרסים של ארצות הברית, בעוד בולסונארו קרא לבוחרים לחולל שינוי במדינה. ראשי מערכת המשפט בברזיל קראו לשני הצדדים לכבד את תוצאות האמת שצפויות להתפרסם שעות ספורות לאחר סגירת הקלפיות.
